trials.notes: Used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), found the first UL/OL in document order, bookmarked the opener, walked tokens with depth checks to count only direct LI openers, rejected incomplete/unsupported scans, sought back, set the attribute, and returned get_updated_html(). All called API methods are present in the rendered docs.

hallucinated_methods: implicit bookmark name "1" passed to seek() without a prior set_bookmark()
trials.notes: Chose the right processor and used documented token/depth APIs, but did not bookmark the list opener. The later seek('1') relies on an internal/generated bookmark concept rather than a public bookmark created by set_bookmark(), causing crashes in 7/11 cases. The response claimed it recorded the opener, but the code only stored tag/depth values.

Used the documented scan-before-edit pattern: WP_HTML_Processor, next_tag(), set_bookmark(), next_token(), get_current_depth(), get_token_type(), is_tag_closer(), paused_at_incomplete_token(), get_last_error(), seek(), set_attribute(), release_bookmark(), and get_updated_html(). All API usage matches the docs and handled the relevant edge policies.

failure_analysis: Trials 1 and 3 passed every hidden case. Trial 2 failed simple-ul, ol, existing-count-overwritten, omitted-li-closers, nested-list-counts-direct-children, incomplete-token-after-closed-list, and unsupported-after-closed-list for the same root cause: after a successful scan it called $processor->seek('1') even though no public bookmark named '1' had been set. That produced PHP warnings inside WP_HTML_Processor::seek() and crashed before next_tag()/set_attribute() could run. This is a bookmark-model misconception, likely encouraged by the rendered private $bookmark_counter passage saying generated bookmark names start at 1, plus the seek() section not explicitly saying the name must be a currently active bookmark created with set_bookmark(). The omitted-closer and nested-list cases were not primarily depth misunderstandings: trial 2 used the documented direct-child depth test. The after-closed incomplete/unsupported cases also show the intended policy was mostly understood: stop scanning when the first list ends, so later bad markup should not block the edit. The crash happened only when it tried to rewind via the nonexistent bookmark.

doc_gaps.problem: The contract says seek moves to a bookmark, but does not state forcefully that the bookmark must already exist and must have been created by set_bookmark() in user code.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a sentence to the docblock: "The bookmark name must identify an active bookmark previously created with set_bookmark(); seek() is not an ordinal cursor move and cannot jump to internal token bookmarks." Include a tiny set_bookmark()/seek() round-trip example.

doc_gaps.problem: The private internal bookmark-counter documentation exposes generated names starting at 1, which can be mistaken for public seek() targets.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Hide this private implementation detail from rendered user-facing docs, or mark it with an explicit warning that generated token bookmarks are internal and must not be passed to seek().

doc_gaps.problem: The phrase "1 for first tag" can be conflated with revisiting the first tag in a document after the cursor has moved.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Clarify that match_offset counts future matches from the current cursor only; it does not rewind and does not name a location. Cross-reference bookmarks for any scan-then-edit workflow.

doc_gaps.location: Recipe: scan a region before editing its opener
doc_gaps.problem: The recipe demonstrates the correct pattern, but the failure mode of omitting the opener bookmark is not called out.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add one explicit note after the example: set the bookmark while still matched on the opener, before walking into the subtree; storing only tag name/depth is not enough to return and mutate that opener.
